rfi.description: Americans voted on Tuesday in pivotal midterm elections with Democrats hoping to seize control of Congress and shatter Donald Trump's grip on Washington for the remainder of his term in the White House.

rfi.description: Students blockaded dozens of high schools across France on Tuesday to maintain pressure on the government over education reforms as trade unions prepared for a nationwide strike later this week.

rfi.description: In Miami’s Little Haiti, a man mourning his mother and struggling to find steady work sees opportunity in Donald Trump’s politics. The president’s false claims about Haitian immigrants have not shaken his support. For the man known as Blood, what matters jus before the midterm elections is the promise of a chance to earn a living.

rfi.description: The United Nations confirmed it had begun the process to end its peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara after Russia and the United States vetoed each other's draft resolutions on extending the 35-year-old deployment.

rfi.title: Nine out of 10 crimes against journalists go unpunished, Unesco says
rfi.description: Monday marks the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes Against Journalists – chosen in memory of Ghislaine Dupont and Claude Verlon, two journalists from Radio France Internationale who were murdered in Mali on 2 November, 2013. According to a report by Unesco, attacks and harassment targeting the press continue to go largely unpunished in Africa and across the globe.

rfi.title: Calls mount to ban French TV channel following racist killing
rfi.description: A petition urging that a French television channel be taken off air gained traction on Monday, after accusations that far-right views it aired contributed to the racist killing of a black man.

rfi.description: Health authorities investigating two suspected Ebola cases in north-eastern Nigeria ​confirmed on Monday that both samples were negative after ‌two rounds of testing.

rfi.title: Miami voters weigh local hardship and America's global role as early voting ends
rfi.description: A massive thunderstorm and flash flood warnings failed to deter voters in Miami as they headed to polling stations on Florida’s final day of early voting ahead of the US midterm elections.

rfi.title: A year after the fall of El Fasher, Sudan's war has left a ghost town in its wake
rfi.description: A year after paramilitary forces at war with the Sudanese army captured the strategic city of El Fasher, survivors and aid workers report that the capital of North Darfur state remains largely abandoned. Some residents are too scared to return, while thousands are still missing – many held in deplorable conditions in overcrowded prisons.

rfi.title: France launches 'attempted murder' probe after petrol bomb attack on police
rfi.description: France has launched an attempted murder investigation after petrol bombs were thrown at security forces during a weekend protest in Paris, prosecutors told AFP on Sunday.

rfi.title: 'Working in Russia is like being a deep-sea diver', BBC's man in Moscow tells RFI
rfi.description: How does one report, from its capital, on the reality of Russia at war? Based in Moscow for more than 30 years, the BBC's Russia correspondent Steve Rosenberg is one of the few Western journalists still working in the country. He spoke to RFI about his daily life as a reporter in Russia and why he has chosen to stay, despite the Kremlin's increasing hostility to foreign media.

rfi.title: Five British anti-immigration activists arrested in northern France
rfi.description: French police say they've arrested five British far-right activists found carrying tear gas bombs, as they were filming themselves harassing migrants near the northern Channel port of Dunkirk.

rfi.title: Florida Keys business owners reveal contrasting views of Trump's America
rfi.description: Two restaurant owners in the Florida Keys have differing views of Donald Trump's America on the eve of US midterm elections, with a French immigrant concerned about growing political divisions and a Cuban-American restaurateur still sympathetic to Republicans despite misgivings about the president.

rfi.title: 'Protecting the Congo's forests means protecting people's lives'
rfi.description: The forests of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo are a haven for some of the world's rarest species – but despite being protected areas, they are under threat from conflict, poaching and deforestation. After global decision-makers gathered at the United Nations' Cop17 biodiversity summit this week, Emmanuel Bahati Lukoo, a ranger at Kahuzi-Biega National Park, says people on the frontline of wildlife protection deserve greater recognition.

rfi.title: Youth Olympics kick off in Senegal with 'magical' opening ceremony
rfi.description: The Youth Olympic Games opened with a spectacular ceremony in Senegal on Saturday, marking the first Olympic event in Africa as the continent seeks a bigger role in international sports competitions.

rfi.title: Why war makes Ukraine media more determined than ever to hold power to account
rfi.description: For Ukrainian media, exposing corruption in times of war is a high-stakes move – with domestic scandals potentially tarnishing the country's image in the eyes of the international partners it relies on. But journalists remain dedicated to their role as a counterbalance to the authorities, believing that upholding democracy is more important now than ever.

rfi.title: 'African leaders are not naive, they will partner with whoever makes the best offer’
rfi.description: The third Russia-Africa Summit took place in Moscow this week, with 48 African nations sending delegations. It comes as Moscow grapples with sanctions and isolation over its Ukraine offensive, while African governments turn to it for security assistance. However, geopolitical analyst Priyal Singh tells RFI that despite this, Russia still lags behind China in its influence on the continent.

lemonde.description: Le Mécanisme européen de stabilité peut prêter jusqu’à 500 milliards d’euros aux pays financièrement étranglés. « Nous n’avons aucune raison d’intervenir à ce stade », assure son directeur général.

lemonde.description: Le président ukrainien, Volodymyr Zelensky, a estimé que plus de 50 personnes pourraient encore se trouver sous les décombres. Sénégal : le budget rectificatif rejeté par les députés
france24fr.description: Dans cette édition, direction le Sénégal, où le rejet du projet de loi de finances par l’Assemblée nationale, malgré un nouveau passage en commission des finances, n’a pas convaincu les députés du Pastef. Une décision qui pourrait compromettre l’obtention d’un prêt de plus de deux milliards de dollars du FMI. En Afrique du Sud, à quelques heures de l’ouverture des bureaux de vote, les électeurs s’apprêtent à choisir leurs nouveaux élus locaux, dans un scrutin marqué par de nombreux défis et des

france24fr.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : L’or pour le Kenya, une première olympique pour l’Afrique en rugby à 7
france24fr.description: 🥇 🇰🇪 Les Kényanes ont remporté le tournoi féminin de rugby à 7 en s’imposant face à l’Australie (17-12). Une première pour une nation africaine dans une compétition olympique. Une victoire historique dans la première édition des JO organisée sur le sol africain.

france24fr.title: Ligue des champions : le PSG en démonstration, Manchester United renversant
france24fr.description: Les Parisiens, doubles tenants du titre, ont plié leur match de mardi en Ligue des champions face à Villareal en moins de huit minutes avec quatre buts de quatre joueurs différents, et restent seuls en tête. Manchester United s’est imposé 3-2 grâce à un doublé de Cunha, tandis que le Barça et le Bayernont gagné et que Lille a concédé un nul à Bodoe/Glimt.

france24fr.title: Espagne : le ministre des Transports démissionne à la suite de l'accident ferroviaire
france24fr.description: Le ministre espagnol des Transports, Oscar Puente, a présenté sa démission mardi, à l'issue d'une comparution devant les députés. Une décision prise à la suite de la collision ferroviaire qui a fait près de 70 morts dans la région de Tolède, le deuxième accident d'ampleur survenu depuis le début de l'année sur le rail espagnol.

france24fr.title: Midterms : Vague bleue sur le Congrès ?
france24fr.description: Des Midterms décisives. 250 millions d'Américains appelés à décider de la marge de manoeuvre dont disposera Donald Trump pour la suite de son mandat, en renouvelant l'intégralité de la Chambre des Représentants et un tiers du Sénat. Décisives, car une vague bleue pourrait bien déferler sur le Congrès. Pourrait car si les sondages prédisent des démocrates vainqueurs à la Chambre des Représentants, la bataille au Sénat sera plus serrée.

france24fr.title: Une série de fausses alertes à la bombe perturbe une dizaine de vols en Europe
france24fr.description: Le ciel européen a été perturbé mardi par une série de fausses alertes à la bombe ayant entraîné l'inspection d'avions et des opérations de déminage. En Hongrie et en Italie, des vols ont été escortés par l'armée. Un paquebot a lui aussi été évacué en Grèce après une fausse alerte.

france24fr.title: Midterms : l'Amérique à l'heure du choix
france24fr.description:
Coup d'envoi ce 3 novembre des élections de mi-mandat aux ETats-Unis. Les électeurs américains se rendent aux urnes afin d'élire les députés de la Chambre des représentants ainsi qu'un tiers du Sénat. Si les démocrates sont favoris pour la chambre basse, la bataille s'annonce bien plus serrée pour le Sénat, où quelques Etats-clés pourraient faire basculer la majorité.
 
Nous vous faisons vivre cette élection en direct avec nos invités et nos envoyés spéciaux.

france24fr.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : Comment circuler dans la capitale sénégalaise ?
france24fr.description: 🚦 À Dakar, les JOJ 2026 mettent la mobilité urbaine au défi. Entre transports publics, circulation et dispositifs spéciaux, comment se déplacer dans la capitale sénégalaise pendant les Jeux ? Un reportage de Alexandrine Holognon.

france24fr.title: Midterms 2026 : la folie des auto-collants 'I voted'
france24fr.description:
#EtatsUnis : c'est l'accessoire tendance en ce moment dans le pays. 
 
Après avoir voté pour les #Midterms, les Américains arborent fièrement un sticker montrant leur participation à ces élections de mi-mandat. 
 
Notre journaliste Valentin Cacheux est parti à la rencontre de certains d'entre eux, à #Detroit, dans le Michigan. 
 
#Midterms2026 #IVoted

france24fr.title: Sarah El Haïry (Modem) : "Les extrêmes alimentent des comportements violents"
france24fr.description: La mobilisation lycéenne, tout en étant moins suivie, se poursuit. Pour Sarah El Haïry, haute-commissaire à l’Enfance, "il faut mettre en œuvre les annonces faites aux lycéens". La vice-présidente du Mouvement démocrate estime que "la jeunesse exprime une angoisse". Après l’attentat raciste de Trappes, les tensions politiques et sociales ont été ravivées. Une poussée qu'elle attribue en partie aux "extrêmes qui alimentent des comportements violents".

Prix Goncourt 2026 : Philippe Jaenada récompensé pour « L'inconnue du quai de Javel »
france24fr.description: Le prix Goncourt 2026 a été attribué à Philippe Jaenada pour « L'inconnue du quai de Javel » (Flammarion). Dans ce roman, l'écrivain français mène une enquête sur un meurtre non élucidé, celui de Louise Cansot, modèle des peintres de Montparnasse, retrouvée morte dans l'ouest parisien.

france24fr.title: En Indonésie, les incendies de forêt attisent la colère des étudiants
france24fr.description: Plusieurs milliers de personnes manifestent depuis fin octobre en Indonésie pour dénoncer la gestion par le gouvernement des incendies de forêts massifs qui touchent le pays et dont les fumées toxiques affectent la santé de la population locale et gagnent les nations voisines comme la Malaisie ou Singapour. Une catastrophe qui intervient dans un contexte social tendu deux ans après l'arrivée au pouvoir du président Prabowo Subianto.

france24fr.title: Pénurie de dermatologues en France : cherche rendez-vous désespérément
france24fr.description: Des délais d'attente à rallonge et des patients qui tentent tout pour obtenir un rendez-vous : la France connaît une pénurie sans précédent de dermatologues. Avec trois pour 100 000 habitants et des départements entiers qui en sont dépourvus, consulter un dermatologue est devenu un parcours du combattant. Près de 200 000 nouveaux cancers sont dépistés chaque année et les besoins ne cessent d'augmenter. Quelles solutions pour lutter contre la pénurie ? Reportage de Sonia Baritello.

france24fr.title: Midterms: La politique climaticide de Donald Trump
france24fr.description: Depuis son retour à la Maison Blanche, Donald Trump démantèle toute la politique climatique des États-Unis. D'abord en coupant les liens de la diplomatie climatique, en quittant l'Accord de Paris, la Convention-cadre de l'ONU sur les changements climatiques et en boycottant les COP. Puis en supprimant les règlementations fédérales, dont le "constat de mise en danger" sur les effets néfastes des émissions, les limitations concernant le méthane ou les émissions des centrales thermiques.

nzz.title: Champions League: Manchester United dreht Partie gegen Roma, Bayern und Inter siegen in der Fremde
nzz.description: In der vierten Runde der Champions-League-Ligaphase siegen die Favoriten.

nzz.title: Reformierte Kirche will Opfern sexuellen Missbrauchs Genugtuung bezahlen
nzz.description: Eine neue Kommission kann Betroffenen bis zu 20 000 Franken zusprechen. Bezahlt wird aber nur, wenn die Taten bereits verjährt sind.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN POLIZEI - Feuerwehreinsatz nach Ammoniakaustritt bei Zürcher Energiezentrale +++ Freiheitsstrafen für zwei Männer nach Ausschreitungen
nzz.description: Die neuesten Polizeimeldungen aus der Schweiz.

nzz.title: «Aufrecht» war die Partei der Corona-Skeptiker und Esoteriker. Jetzt ist sie fünf Jahre alt. Was ist aus ihr geworden?
nzz.description: Noch immer will die Bewegung weder links noch rechts sein. Noch immer hat sie keinen Erfolg.

nzz.title: Der Kanton Zürich macht Fortschritte Richtung Netto-Null – doch neue Pläne könnten am Widerstand gegen Wind- und Wasserkraft scheitern
nzz.description: Die neue Energiestrategie des Regierungsrats basiert auf Wind- und Solarkraft. Aber der Plan, sie auszubauen, stösst auf grossen Widerstand.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Es war ein Fehler, den ukrainischen Flüchtlingen in Deutschland Bürgergeld zu geben
nzz.description: Die deutsche Regierung hat wieder einmal Migranten reichlich unterstützt, aber wenig gefordert. Diese Politik rächt sich jetzt – und strapaziert die Hilfsbereitschaft der Deutschen.

nzz.title: Nach 21 Jahren geht eine grosse Familiensaga zu Ende: Mit Michelle verlässt die Letzte der Familie Gisin den Ski-Weltcup
nzz.description: Die unerschütterliche Liebe zum Skifahren schenkte der Familie aus Engelberg historische Triumphe wie drei Olympiasiege, forderte durch Stürze und Schmerzen aber auch einen Tribut. Die Gisins schweisste dies nur noch enger zusammen.

nzz.title: Angreifer von Belgrad sass wohl zuvor in München in Untersuchungshaft
nzz.description: Ein Wachbeamter wird vor der israelischen Botschaft in Belgrad angegriffen. Der mutmassliche Angreifer war den Behörden in Deutschland bekannt – wegen des Verdachts auf Anschlagspläne in München.

nzz.title: Die Stadt Zürich verliert an bester Lage 127 Parkplätze mit Seesicht
nzz.description: Bald beginnen die Arbeiten an der neuen Promenade beim Hafen Enge.

nzz.title: Der britische Premierminister wagt bei der Frage nach Reparationszahlungen für die Sklaverei eine Flucht nach vorn
nzz.description: Am jährlichen Treffen der Commonwealth-Staaten spricht der britische König sein tiefes Bedauern über den Sklavenhandel aus. Es ist aber Andy Burnham, der zum ersten Mal in der britischen Geschichte eine offizielle Entschuldigung ankündigt.

nzz.title: «Die kleine Märtyrerin von der A 10»: Fast vierzig Jahre nach dem Fund einer Kindsleiche stehen in Frankreich die Eltern vor Gericht
nzz.description: Jahrzehntelang wusste niemand, wer das tote Mädchen war, das an einer Autobahn abgelegt worden war. Erst eine DNA-Spur führte zur Familie von Inass Touloub. Sie wurde nur vier Jahre alt und musste Schreckliches erleiden.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Signa-Insolvenz: René Benko steht erneut vor Gericht
nzz.description: Das Immobilien- und Detailhandelsreich des österreichischen Investors René Benko ist zusammengebrochen. Die Signa-Holding und mehrere Tochtergesellschaften stecken in einem Insolvenzverfahren. Die wichtigsten Fragen und Antworten.

nzz.title: Tausend Parkplätze beim Zoo ersatzlos streichen, dafür eine Tramlinie bis zum Eingang – der VCS zerpflückt die Pläne von Stadt und Kanton
nzz.description: Stadt und Kanton planen für den Zoo ein Parkhaus mit bis zu 1200 Plätzen. Das geht dem grünen Verkehrsclub der Schweiz viel zu weit.

nzz.title: Um die Sicherheit der Schweiz zu stärken: Bundesrat soll Gruppen wie Hamas und Hizbullah schneller verbieten können
nzz.description: Will die Schweiz eine Terrororganisation verbieten, muss sie jeweils ein Spezialgesetz erlassen. Doch präzise Kriterien fehlen, zudem ist dieser Weg langwierig. Nun zeichnet sich ein Systemwechsel ab.

observador.title: As intercalares nos EUA são um referendo a Donald Trump?
observador.description: Paulo do Nascimento Cabral (PSD), Jorge Miguel Teixeira (IL) e Rui Teixeira Santos (CH) focam o voto na carteira. Já João Torres (PS) e Tomás Cardoso Pereira (L) veem uma derrota da extrema-direita.

observador.title: Canadá proíbe entrada de atletas pela Rússia e Bielorrússia
observador.description: Apesar da decisão do Tribunal Arbitral do Desporto, que pretende reintegrar a Rússia nos campeonatos de hóquei, o Canadá proíbe a participação do país e da Bielorrússia no próximo mundial de júniores.

observador.title: Paulo Sande: "Trump já se anunciou como Mr. Veto"
observador.description: Paulo Sande aponta que Donald Trump manterá a linha dura com a Europa mesmo se perder o Congresso. Ainda fala sobre a corrida às presidenciais e o impacto das investigações.

observador.title: Ricardo Ferreira Reis: "Há uma aproximação ao centro"
observador.description: Ricardo Ferreira Reis sublinha que os democratas nas corridas disputadas são mais centristas. O economista também acrescenta que estes resultados vão desenhar o candidato daqui a dois anos.

observador.title: Daniela Melo: "Os ventos são favoráveis aos democratas"
observador.description: Daniela Melo afirma que a inflação e a guerra beneficiam a oposição. A professora de Ciência Política na Universidade de Boston também destaca que intercalares funcionam como um referendo a Trump.

observador.title: Foie gras e transgénero: os referendos nas intercalares
observador.description: Além de elegerem senadores e congressistas, os norte-americanos votam em vários referendos estaduais. As propostas vão do aborto aos direitos dos transgénero, cobrindo o estatuto da caça e foie gras.

observador.title: Activistas anti: mercado, Natal e Mercado de Natal
observador.description: Só faltava a crise da habitação desalojar o Pai Natal. E sobrou para a Câmara lidar com a Cambra: deixar ou tirar a tenda? É fazer moeda ao ar num cara ou coroa e no fim ver se o Moedas foi ao ar

observador.title: Alexandrina Cruz recandidata-se à presidência do Rio Ave
observador.description: De olho num segundo mandato à frente do Rio Ave, Alexandrina Cruz admite preocupação com o 16.º lugar no campeonato, mas garante que o clube de Vila do Conde pode regressar às provas europeias.

observador.title: Fernández Cubas vence o Prémio Cervantes 2026
observador.description: O ministro da Cultura de Espanha anunciou a vencedora do mais prestigiado galardão das letras em espanhol, dotado de 125 mil euros. Será entregue em abril de 2027.

observador.title: Livre, BE e PAN lamentam falta de autocrítica de Montenegro
observador.description: A manutenção da lei do arrendamento e a falta de um pedido de desculpas aos manifestantes pela repressão policial nos protestos das últimas semanas valeram críticas da esquerda parlamentar ao Governo.

observador.title: CNCS acompanha ciberataque a sete lojas Intermarché
observador.description: Três supermercados registaram perda de produtos. Ataque terá tido origem em acesso não autorizado ao controlador remoto de temperatura, via fornecedor externo.

observador.title: Oeste concorre a um dos seis grandes parques empresariais
observador.description: Outeiro da Cabeça é zona proposta para um dos seis parques empresariais do Governo. Projeto estratégico une quatro concelhos, aproveita a A8 e portos marítimos para fixar investimento na região.

observador.title: Jovem morreu enquanto corria a maratona de Nova Iorque
observador.description: Rachel Apa treinou durante meses para a competição. A cinco quilómetros do fim, o seu corpo entrou em falência devido ao excesso de exercício físico. Morreu no hospital após seis horas de reanimação.

observador.title: Os Toyota são sólidos. Para provar atiraram roulote à Hilux
observador.description: Recuperando um episódio do Top Gear de 2003, em que a equipa de Jeremy Clarkson deixou cair uma roulote em cima de uma muito mal tratada pick-up Hilux, a Toyota repetiu a mesma receita 23 anos depois.

observador.title: Ventura defende que lei das rendas seja aprovada com o PS
observador.description: André Ventura defende que a nova lei do arrendamento deve ser aprovada com PSD e PS. Criticou o primeiro-ministro por ausência e falta de empatia durante a crise da habitação.

observador.title: Ex-casal julgado por matar idoso culpa-se um ao outro
observador.description: Arguida diz que ele agrediu a vítima com uma pistola. Ex-marido diz que ela usou um ferro. O casal de 40 anos, em prisão preventiva, responde por homicídio qualificado, roubo e sequestro.

observador.title: Montenegro tenta superar crise com ramo de oliveira
observador.description: Pressionado por Seguro, Montenegro chama Ventura e Carneiro para discutir Habitação. PM recusa que tenha estado em silêncio e que Governo esteja parado. Mas deixa cair braço de ferro com manifestantes

observador.title: Carneiro condiciona acordo nas rendas à boa-fé de Montenegro
observador.description: Líder do PS pronto para ajustar a proposta socialista sobre rendas, mas mantém o arquivamento da proposta do Governo como condição prévia. E aponta "problemas de consciência" a Ventura.

spiegel.title: Chile: Gericht entscheidet im Sorgerechtsstreit um Katze »Perseo«
spiegel.description: Was passiert mit dem gemeinsamen Haustier, wenn ein Paar sich trennt? Mit dieser Frage musste sich jetzt in Chile der oberste Gerichtshof befassen. Es entschied: Das Wohl der Katze ist wichtiger als die Interessen der Besitzer.

spiegel.title: Midterms 2026 in den USA: Frühe Siege lassen Demokraten hoffen
spiegel.description: Die US-Midterms sind in vollem Gange – und die Demokraten legen einen starken Start hin. Ein wichtiger Sieg gelingt ihnen in North Carolina. Im neuen Senat wird erstmals auch ein homosexueller Politiker sitzen. Alle Entwicklungen in der Liveanalyse.

spiegel.title: Verband fordert 500 Euro Bußgeld für Handy am Steuer
spiegel.description: Während der Fahrt das Smartphone in die Hand nehmen – das kann zu schweren Unfällen führen. Verkehrsminister Steffen Bilger macht sich für Handyblitzer stark. Der Verkehrssicherheitsrat hat noch eine andere Idee.

spiegel.title: Mutter getötet und Tochter vermisst – Behörden vermuten Bärenangriff
spiegel.description: Zwei Wanderinnen galten in der kanadischen Wildnis als vermisst, dann machte ein Suchtrupp eine traurige Entdeckung. Als wahrscheinlich gilt eine Grizzly-Attacke – es wäre nicht der erste Fall in der isolierten Region.

spiegel.title: Toni Kroos reagiert auf Jude Bellingham in knapper Unterwäsche
spiegel.description: In einer neuen Werbekampagne ist Fußballer Jude Bellingham in teils sehr engen Unterhosen zu sehen. Mehr als 3,7 Millionen seiner Follower gefällt das. Auch sein ehemaliger Teamkollege Toni Kroos kommentiert die Bilder.

spiegel.title: Formel 1: Haas trennt sich von Esteban Ocon, Brasilianer rückt nach
spiegel.description: In Mexiko wurde er kurzfristig aus dem Cockpit verbannt, jetzt ist für Esteban Ocon endgültig Schluss: Er verliert seinen Platz im Team Haas. Die Hintergründe bleiben nebulös.

spiegel.title: Champions League: PSG stellt Torrekord auf, Yann Bisseck trifft für Inter Mailand
spiegel.description: Während die Dominanz von PSG gegen Villareal für einen neuen Königsklassen-Rekord reicht, gelingt Manchester United ein wichtiger Sieg in der Krise. Und: DFB-Verteidiger Yann Bisseck trifft sehenswert für Inter Mailand.

spiegel.title: Champions League: FC Bayern München schlägt Atlético Madrid locker
spiegel.description: Im Stadion des kommenden Champions-League-Finals lässt der FC Bayern Atlético Madrid keine Chance. Manuel Neuer stellt einen Rekord auf, zwei Defensivleute überragen – und Lennart Karl wird für seinen Torjubel kritisiert.

spiegel.title: Kaiserslautern: Ein toter und ein verletzter Jäger nach Treibjagd
spiegel.description: Im Kreis Kaiserslautern ist ein Jäger auf einem Hochsitz mit einer tödlichen Schussverletzung aufgefunden worden. Während der Jagd wurde zudem ein 29-Jähriger von einem Wildschwein schwer verletzt.

spiegel.title: BMW: Prognose für 2026 erneut gesenkt
spiegel.description: Für das laufende Geschäftsjahr rechnet BMW mit Verlusten im Automobilsegment. Das hat auch mit dem Umbau im Management zu tun.

spiegel.title: Champions League: VfB Stuttgart verliert bei Galatasaray Istanbul und Leroy Sané
spiegel.description: Der in der Champions League bisher so erfolgreiche VfB Stuttgart verliert bei Galatasaray. Vor hitziger Kulisse vergeben die Schwaben selbst beste Chancen. Und auch Leroy Sané darf noch etwas mitspielen.

spiegel.title: Spanien: Verkehrsminister Óscar Puente kündigt nach tödlichem Zugunglücken Rücktritt an
spiegel.description: Im Januar die Katastrophe von Adamuz, zuletzt das Unglück von Toledo mit Dutzenden Toten: Nach Rücktrittsforderungen hat der spanische Verkehrsminister Óscar Puente nun sein Amt niedergelegt.

spiegel.title: Berlin: SPD und Grüne lassen CDU nach Sondierungsangebot abblitzen
spiegel.description: Die Berliner SPD und Grünen sind längst in Koalitionsverhandlungen mit der Linken, und doch drängt CDU-Landeschef Stefan Evers auf Sondierungen mit den Parteien. Trotz deren Ablehnung bleibe »die Hand ausgestreckt«.

spiegel.title: 2. Bundesliga: Frank Schmidt verlässt Heidenheim zum Saisonende
spiegel.description: Frank Schmidt führte den 1. FC Heidenheim von der Oberliga bis in den Europapokal. Nach fast zwei Jahrzehnten schlug der Erfolgstrainer nun eine Vertragsverlängerung aus. Er will ab Sommer erst einmal »Pause machen«.

spiegel.title: Ukraine: Selenskyjs Ex-Sprecherin Julija Mendel wegen Hochverrats angeklagt
spiegel.description: Im Podcast von Tucker Carlson nannte sie Selenskyj einen »boshaften Narzisst«: Julija Mendel soll mit ihren Aussagen die Ukraine diskreditiert haben. Dafür muss die ehemalige Pressesprecherin womöglich lebenslang in Haft.

spiegel.title: Alle Ergebnisse der US-Midterms 2026

phys-org.title: Shared data ecosystem could help scientists explore new biological connections
phys-org.description: Scientists generate vast amounts of research data, but connecting information across studies can be difficult. The NIH Common Fund Data Ecosystem is working to change that by making research data sets from 18 NIH programs easier to find, connect and analyze.

phys-org.title: Digitalization front-runners are more vulnerable to cyberattacks
phys-org.description: For many business leaders, digitalization is associated with promises of greater efficiency and productivity. However, a new study by professor of accounting Jukka Sihvonen from the University of Vaasa, Finland, suggests that increasing digitalization may also raise a company's risk of falling victim to a successful cyberattack. The study has been published in the journal British Journal of Management.

phys-org.title: Study maps Nelore cattle microbiota to reduce methane emissions
phys-org.description: Researchers at the Brazilian Agricultural Research Corporation (EMBRAPA) are studying the relationship between the genetics of Nelore cattle and the microorganisms in their guts (microbiota). Nelore cattle are the most widely raised beef breed in Brazil. The goal is to develop strategies that reduce emissions of methane—a major greenhouse gas—and improve the animals' feed efficiency.

phys-org.title: North Atlantic's 'cold blob' may contain climate nuance
phys-org.description: Climate observers have long tied the strength of a major ocean current to water temperatures in the so-called "cold blob" in the North Atlantic Ocean. The 965,000-square-mile (2.5 million square kilometers) area south and southeast of Greenland cooled by as much as 1.8 degrees Fahrenheit over the past century as other ocean waters warmed.

phys-org.title: How the nasal microbiome can help potentially harmful bacteria thrive
phys-org.description: Our noses are home to many different species of bacteria living side by side. One of them may be S. aureus. Many people carry this bacterium without knowing it, although it can cause serious infections. Why S. aureus colonizes some people persistently but not others remains only partly understood.

phys-org.title: Semiautomated platform delivers consistent batches of extracellular vesicles for potential regenerative therapies
phys-org.description: A study led by researchers from the Germans Trias i Pujol Research Institute (IGTP) and the Blood and Tissue Bank (BST) has developed and validated a manufacturing platform for extracellular vesicles that meets pharmaceutical quality requirements, marking a key step toward their clinical application.

phys-org.title: US midterm elections: Younger politicians could strengthen trust in democracy
phys-org.description: It's no secret that American politics is dominated by older politicians. When 81-year-old Joe Biden withdrew from the 2024 presidential race amid concerns about his age, it was the then-78-year-old Donald Trump who ultimately entered the White House. The median age in the House of Representatives and the Senate was 58 and 65, respectively, while the average American was just 39 years old.

phys-org.title: Using vibrations to reveal what lies beneath other planets' surfaces
phys-org.description: Modern space exploration hasn't quite reached "Star Trek" levels of boldly going where no one has gone before. But if, like the denizens of the USS Enterprise, astronauts one day want to land on an uncharted planet, they'd first want to know what's on—and under—the surface.

phys-org.title: Tiny fossils show brittle stars gathered around a dead whale 9.5 million years ago
phys-org.description: Tiny skeletal plates recovered beside fossil whale bones in southern Denmark offer a rare glimpse of life around a whale carcass approximately 9.5 million years ago. Researchers have identified a new species of brittle star, Ophiura huebnerjenseni, from the Gram Clay Pit and suggest it represents the first fossil record of brittle stars associated with a whale fall.

phys-org.title: Disillusion runs deep among young Americans, poll reveals
phys-org.description: The kids are not all right on the future. For the first time in the 26-year history of the Harvard Youth Poll, more respondents expect to be worse off financially than their parents (27%) than better off (25%).

phys-org.title: Southern Ocean waters reveal distinct nutrient recycling pathways during decades-long journeys north
phys-org.description: The Southern Ocean may seem far removed from the North Pacific or the Gulf of Maine, but its waters are linked to all the world's major ocean basins through a vast circulation system.

phys-org.title: Asymmetric atomic structure improves sodium–sulfur battery performance
phys-org.description: Chinese researchers have developed a new way to improve sodium–sulfur battery performance by changing the atomic structure of a catalyst. Led by professors Wang Hui and Zheng Fangcai from the High Magnetic Field Laboratory at the Hefei Institutes of Physical Science of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, the study is published in Angewandte Chemie.

phys-org.title: Finding the fingerprints of noisy distributions in random quantum systems
phys-org.description: Imagine shuffling a deck of cards where some of the cards are fading just because of the way they interact with the external environment as you shuffle them. Your job is to figure out the interplay between the shuffling, or "imposed randomness," due to the way you shuffle your cards and how that relates to the fading as cards are exposed to the external environment.

phys-org.title: Tijuana River pollution doesn't stay put—it can travel seven times farther than expected
phys-org.description: Waste dumped into the Tijuana River can travel seven times farther than expected before becoming airborne and affecting San Diego's air, at least 20 miles (32 kilometers) from its source, according to new UC Riverside research.

phys-org.title: New framework helps turn biodiversity goals into measurable action
phys-org.description: The new study by Newcastle University and the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) offers a practical roadmap for tracking progress toward halting species extinctions by 2050. It guides users from understanding where species are most at risk in a given area, through taking action to reduce species threats, to measuring the real-world impact of conservation efforts on reducing species extinction risk over time.

phys-org.title: Cooking is a bigger source of harmful air particles than vehicle exhausts in London and Beijing
phys-org.description: There have been decades of regulations to make vehicles greener and improve air quality in London and Beijing, as well as a popular shift toward less polluting road transport. Now, total emissions of harmful air pollutants from vehicle exhausts are lower than those from cooking in the centers of these two megacities, a study has found.

phys-org.title: Body size, not competition, may kick-start evolution
phys-org.description: A new evolutionary theory suggests changes in body size, rather than competition for food and habitat, may drive the earliest physical differences between species.

undark.title: Body Snatchers and the Murky Process of Whole-Body Donation
undark.description: Opinion | Each year, more than 20,000 people in the U.S. donate their bodies to science after death. But the programs that handle whole-body donations lack oversight, with inconsistencies in standards of consent, transparency, and accountability. The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.title: Book Review: The Bizarre Frontiers of Product Testing
undark.description: From rampaging bears to zero-G toilets and chicken cannons, Alex Davies, in “Kobuk the Destroyer,” chronicles the surprising and often bizarre world of test engineering, and the ingenious lengths to which product testers will go to make the world a safer place.

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
undark.description: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?
undark.description: Brazil has plans to repave a neglected 550-mile road in the South American rainforest to help connect the region and boost economic growth. But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds
undark.description: This year’s spring migration in North America unveiled real-time measures at a higher resolution than ever before. On one night, for instance, 156 million birds appeared in the skies, outpacing the forecasted total by 20 million. And researchers figured that out thanks to AI.

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency
undark.description: After years of limited oversight, the FDA sent warnings to more than 2,200 clinical trial sponsors about missing results, which were supposed to be uploaded to an official public database. Experts have pushed for greater transparency.

undark.title: Book Review: An Optimistic Defense of Uncertainty in Science
undark.description: At an uncertain moment in the sciences, Stuart Firestein argues in favor of optimism in “It Could Be Otherwise,” since uncertainty leaves room for possibility, and possibility drives curiosity, imagination, and the agency to study the peculiarities of the natural world.

undark.title: The New Importance of the Scientific Seminar
undark.description: Opinion | The rise of artificial intelligence in science complicates the notion of expertise. When AI can be used to generate ideas, conduct research, and write papers, live scientific presentations — such as public talks and seminars — become more important as a way to demonstrate who is a real expert and who is not.

proj-syn.title: Oligarchic World Order
proj-syn.description: Today, some 64 heads of state or government are oligarchs, leading countries that together account for some 60% of global GDP. The question is thus no longer whether oligarchs will rule the world, but rather what kind of world they are building.

proj-syn.title: Poland’s Constitutional Civil War
proj-syn.description: Polish right-wing populists recently stormed the country's Constitutional Tribunal, winning applause from the Kremlin and far-right fellow-travelers across Europe. As in other countries, the constitutional tribunal is the institution that distinguishes a proper democracy from a dictatorship making it a target for authoritarians.

proj-syn.title: The Tech Brotherhood Wants Sovereignty
proj-syn.description: After centuries of nation-states, a new form of sovereignty is asserting itself. The small fraternity that controls the major digital platforms has already proven capable of even more intrusive and insidious forms of control than most states can muster.

proj-syn.title: The Far Right’s Vision for Europe
proj-syn.description: In many ways, Europe’s far right has already won, regardless of what happens at the ballot box in the coming months. Its parties may still quarrel among themselves, but they agree on the three big issues that will define much of the European political agenda for years to come.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Bright Future
proj-syn.description: A narrative of European decline has taken hold, and if the EU continues on its current path, it may well materialize. But this is not a foregone conclusion: Europe retains considerable strengths on which it can build as it pursues critical reforms aimed at unleashing innovation.

proj-syn.title: A Debtors’ Club for a Fragmented World
proj-syn.description: The newly created Borrowers’ Platform aims to facilitate knowledge-sharing and capacity-building among debtor countries, while amplifying their voices in global financial circles. But at a time when the Paris Club of sovereign creditors is increasingly unable to act collectively, the Borrowers’ Platform should ramp up its ambition.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Tariff Fiasco Could Save Free Trade
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump’s tariffs have raised prices and hurt businesses without reducing the trade deficit or creating manufacturing jobs. But global trade has held up better than expected, and growing public opposition to tariffs could pave the way for a retreat from protectionism.

proj-syn.title: If AI Thinks for Us, Democracy Will Suffer
proj-syn.description: Whereas the internet buried us in information, AI enables us to outsource analysis altogether. But when it comes to grappling with humanity’s most important questions, we must resist the temptation and recognize that we all have a duty—to each other and to ourselves—to keep “showing up.”

proj-syn.title: A Tory Mentor for the MAGA GOP
proj-syn.description: Kemi Badenoch’s keynote address at the British Conservative Party conference last month outlined her plan for a pro-growth future that respects fiscal discipline and human dignity. As American conservatives look beyond Donald Trump and to the 2028 primary campaign, they should embrace a similar agenda.

proj-syn.title: The Politics of Poland’s Judicial Crisis
proj-syn.description: The removal of Bogdan Święczkowski as president of the Constitutional Tribunal has triggered a physical confrontation at the court and a political standoff between Donald Tusk’s government and the far-right Law and Justice (PiS) party. But Święczkowski was not so much removed as barred, because he held the position illegally.

proj-syn.title: Mapping AI Resistance
proj-syn.description: Since a society that is reluctant to deploy a technology will not capture its gains, it is worth understanding why the AI revolution is being welcomed in some places and resisted in others. The explanation is not as simple as headline poll data and much media coverage suggest.

proj-syn.title: The World’s Perilous Ebola Complacency
proj-syn.description: The exponential trajectory of the latest Ebola outbreak is an urgent reminder that infectious diseases do not wait for ideal geopolitical alignments or balanced budgets. Global leaders must fund the Africa-led regional response today, or risk paying an immeasurably higher price in human lives and economic devastation tomorrow.

proj-syn.title: Industrial Decarbonization Is Good for Business
proj-syn.description: With major governments showing open hostility toward climate solutions or focusing on other needs, one might think that progress toward decarbonization is in jeopardy. Yet across the global industrial sector, many companies are increasing productivity, boosting revenue growth, and reducing emissions all at once.

proj-syn.title: When the AI Bubble Bursts
proj-syn.description: Speculative bubbles often leave behind valuable infrastructure while bankrupting the investors who financed them. AI could follow the same path, but the industry’s growing reliance on borrowed money raises the risk of a major financial crisis long before its world-beating applications emerge.

proj-syn.title: After Brazil and Serbia’s Elections
proj-syn.description: The recent electoral defeat of far-right forces in Brazil and Serbia offers important lessons for pro-democracy forces around the world as they confront nationalist and illiberal movements. But no single election can guarantee democracy’s resilience, and the challenges these countries’ new governments face remain formidable.

proj-syn.title: The New Geopolitics of Mining
proj-syn.description: While the US and China want their critical-mineral investments to deliver the biggest returns possible, governments in resource-rich countries must balance external pressures with internal demands. Mining firms must also win local communities’ trust, as host countries will be quick to throw them under the bus if public opinion sours.

proj-syn.title: Can Bond Vigilantes Prevent the Next Debt Crisis?
proj-syn.description: With interest rates on government debt having gone from near zero to much higher levels in recent years, rising short- and long-term bond yields have cast doubt on the sustainability of some debts and led many to wonder if a crisis might be looming. While some countries are more protected than others, none is immune.

crunchbase.title: More Money, Fewer Checks: These 3 Charts Show The Divide Behind VC’s Record Funding Year
crunchbase.description: Record venture funding in 2026 has been increasingly concentrated in massive AI rounds, while seed- and early-stage deal counts are on the decline. Using Crunchbase data we provide a look at how third-quarter funding continued the year's dollars-up-but-deals-down trend.

crunchbase.title: Series B Funding Is Up, But Fewer Deals Are Getting Done

crunchbase.title: Jumbo Series A Rounds Hiding The Real Squeeze On Seed Startups
crunchbase.description: AI megarounds are masking a shrinking Series A market, leaving seed founders facing higher revenue expectations and longer timelines despite larger seed checks. To improve their chances, MGV's Marc Schröder says, founders should size their seed funding around Series A milestones.

crunchbase.title: The Invisible Graph: How Companies Grow Revenue And Still Lose Value
crunchbase.description: Revenue growth does not guarantee a larger exit, as declining valuation multiples can outweigh operating gains and reduce enterprise value. Guest author Itay Sagie suggests that founders and boards should track valuation alongside financial performance, model the effects of delaying a sale, and begin M&A preparation while the business is strong and buyer interest is favorable.
